answer: Custody is bound to one serial history per identity, and the release schedule rewards depth of a single chain rather than the number of chains, so splitting a chain into siblings destroys the compounding the schedule was meant to reward. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The vertex is the serial tenure, the sable the custody window that must elapse, and the nadir the standing released at the end of it; the vertex is personal, the sable is not skippable, and the nadir cannot be inherited by a sibling.
